report.objective: For every mechanism in scope, analyze the runtime contract after adoption: tools, capabilities, permissions, delegation scope, and authority granted to the agentic component; identify the artifact, result, log, or other evidence it returns and how the outer harness consumes it. findings.claim: The normal implementation Worker is granted harness-defined function tools, with authority split between direct repository navigation, source writes, and a single verification command. list_files/read_file are rooted at target-app; write_file is constrained to target-app/src; run_command accepts only exactly npm test with cwd target-app. Path resolution and command allowlisting are enforced by the outer harness, not by model choice.

An implementation episode is not itself workflow authority: AgentRunResult explicitly distinguishes a terminal model response from verified workflow completion, and says verified completion is owned by the outer harness. The loop records diffs, tool/model counts, discovery, token use, research delegations, and A2A delegations; the outer workflow retains VERIFY/REVIEW and success decisions.

The optional research-child/subagent mechanism grants only list_files, read_file, and submit_evidence_report. Child instructions prohibit writing, shell commands, implementation, repair, review, delegation, and workflow decisions. It has a bounded turn budget, and the parent records child model/tool calls, token usage, inspected paths, report, outcome, failure reason, duration, and workspace root.

Research evidence is admitted only as a structured EvidenceReport whose cited evidence paths must be observed reads; invalid reports, max-turn exhaustion, and model errors are explicit outcomes. The parent receives formatted advisory output and retains implementation authority. Experiment logic explicitly says a correct EvidenceReport proves mechanism correctness, not adoption, and does not make subagents default.

The multi-agent investigation swarm has stronger outer authority boundaries: the Lead may propose only worker IDs/objectives/scope hints. Admission rejects fields that attempt to set model, tools, turn limits, worker counts, delegation, rounds, write access, or read/delegation policy. Harness policy fixes 2–3 workers, one round, read-only workers, no worker delegation, worker/lead/synthesis turn caps, and baseline cap.

Swarm workers receive repository-root list_files/read_file plus submit_investigation_report; execution rejects denied tools and only executes the advertised tools. Workers cannot write, run commands, delegate, or spawn workers. Their report is accepted only when every cited evidence path was actually read. The outer harness runs children in a wave, then synthesizes from admitted reports/failure markers and enforces incomplete-coverage uncertainty when children fail.

The MCP repo-read mechanism replaces the implementation Worker's direct read_file with one host-admitted repo_read_file tool after protocol negotiation and schema validation. The host allowlist admits only that name; it rejects non-allowlisted tools, unsupported capabilities, schemas exposing root/credentials/tokens, schemas with extra properties, or schemas lacking required string path. The MCP server receives an absolute host-configured root via environment, refuses OPENAI_API_KEY, and only reads UTF-8 files under that root. The Worker still retains write_file and npm test through the normal direct harness, while the host retains root selection, protocol/allowlist admission, and closure.

The A2A remote-impact mechanism is explicitly bounded advisory delegation. The Worker can pass only objective and scope; it cannot choose endpoint, filesystem root, credentials, protocol, or security policy, and its result is not Spec, permission, verification, review, or workflow success. Delegation is implementation-only and limited to one remaining delegation. The host validates scope before sending, supplies a separately named remote API key, starts a localhost child with an environment allowlist, and stops it afterward.

A2A admission requires an expected agent name, advertised impact skill, compatible 1.0 protocol, expected localhost interface URL, and HTTP+JSON binding. The host then sends an objective/scope data message, requires a Task (not Message), polls up to three times, requires terminal TASK_STATE_COMPLETED, extracts an ImpactAnalysis artifact, and scope-validates every returned path. Accepted evidence is formatted to the Worker as advisory text; all records carry grantsWorkflowSuccess:false, and failures include discovery/admission/client/transport/task/artifact outcomes.

The remote A2A component itself is read-only and bounded: its instructions and tool schema permit only list_files, read_file, and submit_impact_analysis for a requested scope, with a four-turn cap; it cannot write, run commands, verify, review, or decide workflow success. The remote server is localhost-only, rejects inherited OPENAI_API_KEY, gets an absolute allowed root from the host, and publishes a task lifecycle plus JSON ImpactAnalysis artifact in an in-memory task store. The host is the component that admits or rejects that artifact and decides whether to expose it as evidence.

Fan-out implementation, where enabled by an experiment, gives each child a harness-created git workspace at an exact common base revision; child configs are bound to those workspaces. Child artifacts include source delta, changed files, review diff, scoped verification result, repair attempts, timings, calls, and token usage. The outer harness refuses fan-in after child verification failure, checks exact base provenance, applies deltas in declared integration order, and reports conflicts/lost changes; therefore children have workspace-local write authority but outer integration retains acceptance and merge authority.

Structured investigation reports separate capabilities/evidence from retainedOuterAuthority, durable support, and default status. Final reports are schema-validated, evidence paths are checked against admitted reads, and failed swarm workers force explicit incomplete-coverage uncertainty rather than silently granting full coverage.

Identify gaps, dead paths, ambiguous flags, and incomplete repository coverage, with path-backed evidence.

findings.claim: Default execution is intentionally in-memory/non-durable: runV1Harness only enters durable lifecycle when options.durable is supplied, while the architecture explicitly says default runV1Harness remains in-memory. Durable mode is therefore opt-in, not config/env default.

Opt-in durable workflow has a bounded, file-backed lifecycle: spec_required -> implementation_ready -> review_ready -> terminal, with parsed schema, atomic replacement, fail-closed loading, and authoritative lease/fencing checks on saves.

Durable resume is checkpoint-bound rather than mid-episode: implementation_ready resumes implementation; review_ready resumes independent review while reusing verified workspace and review baseline; there is no phase for mid-Worker or mid-VERIFY recovery.

Durability coverage is explicit: tests cover missing/corrupt/unsupported state, atomic replacement, crash-before/after persistence, workspace mismatch, terminal resume rejection, and rejection of ambiguous experimental modes; CHK01 assertions require no Worker or pre-review VERIFY rerun after review_ready.

Retry is bounded and harness-owned, but durable retry persistence is narrower: retry.ts supports spec/worker/verify/review kinds, while executeReviewWithRetry is the implemented durable executor and WorkflowState only permits retry state on review_ready. Worker mutation is explicitly not retry-safe.

Review retry semantics are persisted before execution and fail-closed: transient failures may retry within DEFAULT_MAX_REVIEW_RETRY_ATTEMPTS=2; semantic/permanent/ambiguous failures stop or require reconciliation; unknown model_error is not treated transient. Tests cover operation IDs, persisted admission, pause/resume, budget exhaustion, and no Worker/pre-review VERIFY rerun.

Lease ownership prevents concurrent durable invocations and fences state writes, but the default 30-minute TTL has no automatic heartbeat; renewal exists as an exported primitive but is not invoked by runV1Harness or delivery execution. A long operation can lose authority and have its later commit rejected.

The local mutex/lease design limits durability to single-machine/local-filesystem semantics, not distributed queue or exactly-once execution: documentation says the lease is not a scheduler, expiry does not stop an old process, and stale side-effect reconciliation is not implemented.

Post-terminal GitHub delivery is a separate opt-in durable mechanism with DeliveryState phases, atomic owned persistence, deterministic agent branch, no force-push/merge, exact-head CI admission, and at most one semantic CI repair. WorkflowState fencing does not fence external GitHub side effects, leaving a documented check-to-external-action race.

Verified repository memory is opt-in and persists independent records, but remains advisory and cannot modify WorkflowState; durable workflow mode rejects memory retrieval/promotion to avoid resume ambiguity. Memory is persistent data, not execution checkpoint/retry state.

Experimental mechanisms are activation-gated and generally non-durable: previous_response_id is selectable while manual replay is default; Planner, research subagents, decomposition, and bounded fan-out are off/conditional by default. Durable mode rejects experimental modes that would make resume ambiguous, and the invocation runner explicitly chooses manual conversation state.

Model routing is conditional rather than a durable execution mechanism: configured model is default, optional OPENAI_REPAIR_MODEL applies only to repair, and no persisted provider conversation/session history is part of WorkflowState. A resumed run reconstructs workflow artifacts but not an interrupted model episode.

Deterministic VERIFY is authoritative evidence but not independently checkpointed as an executable queue/job: normal repair is in-process and bounded, while durable review_ready stores only a passed verification summary plus workspace fingerprint/baseline. Crash during verification must be reconciled by rerunning from the prior checkpoint, not resumed exactly.

uncertainties: No scheduler, queue, worker daemon, or external database implementation was found in inspected files; cross-process job delivery beyond explicit fresh-invocation probes is not established.
Lease renewal is implemented as an API but invocation is not evident in inspected files; production heartbeat behavior is not established.

The large run.ts body was truncated by the read harness, so exact behavior of every durable branch/stopAfter path was not independently traced line-by-line; conclusions rely on state/probe/invocation contracts and architecture documentation.

Documentation describes GitHub delivery as opt-in, but inspected README only documents normal benchmark startup and does not expose a user-facing delivery command/default configuration; activation discoverability is incomplete.

Experimental Planner/subagent/decomposition/fan-out mechanisms have source and architecture status, but persistence behavior outside durable-mode rejection is not established as resumable; treat them as non-durable experiments unless a dedicated probe says otherwise.
